tagline: Down the Yadkin to a lake that swallowed the old road.
intro: NC 268 leaves US 321 north of Lenoir and follows the Yadkin River down out of the mountains into the foothills, northeast through Happy Valley and the pastures and farms around Ferguson, then along the south shore of W. Kerr Scott Reservoir to Wilkesboro. It is 26.3 miles, about 35 minutes.

The Yadkin rises near Blowing Rock and, a long way downstream, becomes the Pee Dee. When the dam was finished in 1962 the highway was moved south of the new lake. Most of the old road went under the water.

moments.title: Fort Defiance
moments.text: General William Lenoir's two-story frame house, with a wing added in 1823, stands on the Yadkin where troops built Fort Isaacs in the summer of 1776.

moments.title: Ferguson
moments.text: A post office on NC 268, with the graves of Tom Dula and two others from a murder case that went into song, and a museum that keeps a Tom Dooley day.

moments.title: W. Kerr Scott Reservoir
moments.text: The road follows the south shore of a lake built to stop the Yadkin's floods, 56 miles of shoreline with the old highway somewhere beneath it.
